label: late original-phase input of n/c/f/s/w/q/l (also z/x/1), suppressed when sequence starts with one of them
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (>99.9% of mass); never at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Rate rises with position (orig_idx 1: 3%, orig_idx 8: 32%) and with L, so mass sits on the last few inputs before <DEL>. Token-selective: strongest on inputs n, c, f (20-24% rate), then s, w, q, l, weaker on z, x, 1; first occurrences are favored (87% of mass has in_first=1). Context modulates it: sequences starting with p/i/g/o/m/j/t have higher rates, and it is weaker when the favored tokens have already shown up earlier (for example as the first token). The top activations (~0.34) are runs of favored tokens at the end of length-8/9 inputs (e.g. ...s c n <DEL>). The predicate gets dev F1 0.58 and mass recall 0.81; the leftover is graded dependence on history that does not reduce to a simple rule.
